description.narrative: Projektet sträcker sig över tre år (2022-2025) med det övergripande målet att stödja utvecklingen av en modern datahanteringsstandard och kapacitetsbyggande aktiviteter för fysisk, urban och hållbar planering i Serbien. Detta stöd är ämnat att lägga grunden för en mer effektiv, transparent och deltagande styrningsmodell. Implementeringen av projektet kommer ske genom samarbete mellan de serbiska och svenska myndigheterna RGA och Lantmäteriet.

The project is a three-year intervention (2022-2025) with the overall goal to support development of a modern data management standards and capacity building activities for spatial and urban plans and sustainable planning in Serbia. Support provided within this contribution is expected to lay the foundation for a more efficient, effective, transparent, and participatory governance model. The contribution will be implemented in cooperation between Serbian and Swedish authorities: RGA and Lantmäteriet.

The overall purpose of the eSpace reform is to integrate all national digital registers important for the place-based approach (based on geospatial location and related data) to sustainable development, and to provide access to data and services when, where and how citizens, businesses and public bodies may need them.
The expected outcomes of the proposed project are the following: Outcome 1: RGA has developed a strategic action plan, established cooperation with stakeholders at central and local government level, and developed capacity to lead the establishment of the ePlan system. Outcome 2: A Pilot database with verified digitalization tools, methodologies, and pilot data for responding to the INSPIRE Directive obligation and SDGs integration in the area of land use planning and management that is made available for all stakeholders. Outcome 3: A Pilot database with verified digitalisation tools, methodology and pilot data for storing and accessing information on legal regimes for land use planning and development is developed and functional. Outcome 4: Organizational structure for ePlan system implementation is established, all stakeholders (government institutions at central and local level) are informed and aware about ePlan system benefits for participatory and transparent sustainable development.

sector.narrative: Public sector policy and administrative management

description.narrative:
The project was launched in January, 2023 and this Conclusion of Performance is based on the achievements made in the second year of implementation, as presented in the Second Annual Report submitted by partners, as well as presentation made at the Second Annual Review meeting, held in April 2025.
Progress of the project can be summarized in the following way:- - Capacities of the Serbian cities and municipalities, as the major stakeholders, were identified and Projects activities and outputs for reaching the defined goals at the end of 2025 were adjusted and modified accordingly. Based on the assessment, a decision was made to establish RGA as a 'host' for all services that will be provided by local self-governments. The uneven development (and in some cases underdevelopment) of local capacities was the key factor that determined this position. - Local stakeholders, planning documents, standards, methodology and action plan for a piloting INSPIRE compliant Land Use data set in Serbia were decided and launched. - Action plan for RGA platforms technical improvements for the enhanced accessibility and functionality was prepared and approved for implementation in 2025. - New system for the sustainable land use planning and development named, Smart Parcel was designed and tendered, which will together with the INSPIRE compliant Land Use dataset support directly achievement of the planned outputs and outcome for Component 2 and Project aim in general. - Major tasks and steps towards improvement of the geodetical framework in Serbia were taken, and will continue in 2025. - Training of the top level RGA staff followed by the analysis of the organisational requirements, adequate implementation tools and internal processes.
In addition, using current achievements of this projects, but also plans and projections for the coming years, RGA is working closely with a handful of other institutions who are seen as relevant partners and users of data produced by RGA. Some of those institutions are: Ministry of Environment, Ministry of Construction and Civil Engineering, Ministry of Interior/Department for Disaster Risk Reduction and others.
All four project components have achieved satisfactory results during 2024. The challenges faced during 2024 included the need to adapt this project and its activities and results to the legal framework changes in domain relevant for the project outcome. Other challenges are the lack of capacity at the LSGs, including lack of tools, staff and knowledge. These challenges where possible to overcome thanks to the strong partnership and trustful cooperation established between the RGA and Lantmäteriet, proved to be the critical success factor for project sustainability.
The RGA is through the partnership with Lantmäteriet and support provided within this project continuously using digitalization as a tool not only in making its work more transparent and efficient but also for combating corruption. According to the latest World Bank global report, Serbia ranked fourth out of 85 countries in terms of efficiency and digital transformation of land registries. During 2024, RGA has reviewed its internal processes with the aim of preventing bribery and corruption. As a preventative measure RGA conducted certification the organization in accordance with the requirements and guidance set by ISO standard 37001:2016 Anti-bribery management systems. The certification and initial audit review was carried out on site at the premises of RGA and certificate issued during December 2024. This phase of the process has also been supported by the current project ePlan4eSpace SmartSDI". It is apparent that the anti-corruption capacity is strengthened through the more transparent share of data. Therefore, project supported digitalisation and implementation within the domain of urban planning in Serbia. That is, by the selected urban plans land use data digitalisation and their publication via the planned digital platform SmartSDI along with other geospatial information important for the efficient and sustainable land development and management on the local level. The subject will also be covered and included in project followup questionnaires to participating municipalities (2025).
In general, taking into account different types of the anti-corruption measures, as well as planned results within this Project, the anti-corruption measures expected to be produced by the Component 2 results would fall into the domain of preventive ones, since planned urban plans data digitalisation and their publication through the digital platform would increase transparency of the tasks entrusted by the law to the various public sectors on all level, both vertically and horizontally. In addition, it is expected that these Project results would directly or indirectly support improvement of existing and development of the new e-government and other digital public services in Serbia.
